english: In one round, three letters are placed at random into three envelopes addressed to their three recipients, one letter in each envelope, all $3!$ placements being equally likely. A round is called a miss if no letter is placed in its correctly addressed envelope. Six rounds are performed independently. The probability that no two consecutive rounds are both misses is $\dfrac{k}{3^{6}}$. Then the value of $k$ is ______.
hindi: एक चक्र में तीन पत्र, उनके तीन प्राप्तकर्ताओं के पते लिखे तीन लिफाफों में यादृच्छया रखे जाते हैं, प्रत्येक लिफाफे में एक पत्र, तथा सभी $3!$ व्यवस्थाएँ समसम्भाव्य हैं। एक चक्र को चूक कहा जाता है यदि कोई भी पत्र अपने सही पते वाले लिफाफे में नहीं रखा जाता। छह चक्र स्वतन्त्र रूप से किए जाते हैं। कोई भी दो क्रमागत चक्र दोनों चूक न होने की प्रायिकता $\dfrac{k}{3^{6}}$ है। तब $k$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Let $b_{n}=P(\text{no two consecutive misses in } n \text{ rounds})$. Split on the first round: not a miss, or a miss followed by a non-miss
solution_full: One round: of the $3!=6$ placements, the derangements are the two cyclic placements, so $D_{3}=3!\left(1-1+\dfrac{1}{2!}-\dfrac{1}{3!}\right)=2$ and $P(\text{miss})=\dfrac{1}{3}$, $P(\text{not a miss})=\dfrac{2}{3}$. Rounds are independent.

Recursion: let $b_{n}$ be the probability that among $n$ rounds no two consecutive rounds are both misses ($b_{0}=b_{1}=1$). Condition on the first round. If it is not a miss (probability $\dfrac{2}{3}$), the remaining $n-1$ rounds must have the property: $\dfrac{2}{3}b_{n-1}$. If it is a miss (probability $\dfrac{1}{3}$), the second round must not be a miss (probability $\dfrac{2}{3}$) and the remaining $n-2$ rounds must have the property: $\dfrac{2}{9}b_{n-2}$.
originality_note: New: a repeated matching experiment in which each round is a miss with the derangement probability 1/3, and the 'no two consecutive misses' probability is computed by a weighted Fibonacci-type recursion c_n = 2c_{n-1} + 2c_{n-2} (way 5: derangement probability linked with a recursion). Closest known: NCERT 'three letters in three envelopes, probability none correct' and 'no two consecutive heads in n tosses' (Fibonacci). Different because: the success probability comes from a derangement and the recursion has unequal weights, so neither standard result applies alone.
blueprint_concepts: Probability problems requiring recursion or an infinite series

concept_use.Derangement and matching probability pro: P(miss) = D3/3! = 1/3 is the matching (derangement) probability for three letters.
concept_use.Probability problems requiring recursion: The probability for six rounds is found from the recursion b_n = (2/3)b_{n-1} + (2/9)b_{n-2}.
